title: Detecting Borderline Personality Disorder from Reddit
abstract: We present a transformer-based approach to detecting BPD signals in social media text.
ai_reason: Directly relevant to BPD detection from social media.
methodology: The authors fine-tune a transformer-based model on a Reddit corpus, evaluating against a held-out test set drawn from BPD-related subreddits.
findings: The model achieves competitive recall and precision against a CNN baseline, with attention visualisations highlighting affective language as the strongest predictive signal.
relevance: Directly relevant to the student's BPD detection thesis, particularly the use of attention-based architectures on Reddit text.
limitations: Single-subreddit training and absence of demographic controls limit generalisability.

title: Hierarchical Attention Networks for Mental Health NLP
abstract: We extend HANs with feature-guided attention biases for clinical NLP tasks.
ai_reason: Hierarchical attention work overlaps with the student's HAN extensions.
methodology: The authors propose feature-guided attention biases injected at both word and sentence level within a hierarchical attention network.
findings: Adding the feature bias improves macro-F1 over the HAN baseline across two clinical NLP datasets.
relevance: Provides a recipe for incorporating external features into HAN attention scores, directly aligned with the student's MentalBERT HAN work.
limitations: Evaluation is restricted to two datasets and the gain over baseline is modest.
